name: Caps slide through the crossing
aliases: naturality of the crossing for the cap
summary: A wire crossing both legs of a cap can be moved off the cap.
description:
The *crossing* (fermionic swap) of the ZW-calculus is the map $|00\rangle\langle 00| + |01\rangle\langle 10| + |10\rangle\langle 01| - |11\rangle\langle 11|$: a swap that picks up a sign $-1$ when two $|1\rangle$'s (two fermions) are exchanged. It equals a SWAP followed by a CZ. It behaves like a symmetric braiding, except that it is only natural for *even* maps (those whose terms all have an even number of 1s); maps of odd parity, such as the black vertices, pick up signs. 

The upside-down version of [cups slide through the crossing](../fermionic-crossing-cup/): the cap is even, so a wire crossing both of its legs can be pulled off it.
unchecked_reason: uses the fermionic crossing of the ZW-calculus, which is not a PyZX generator; bare caps cannot be drawn with ZXLive-style boundaries
